core: Human origins: anatomically modern Homo sapiens evolved in Africa (~300,000 years ago per Smithsonian; some texts say ~200,000)
Out-of-Africa migration of Homo sapiens as a global process over tens of thousands of years
The Paleolithic Age: nomadic hunter-gatherer bands, foraging, stone tools, control of fire, early art
The Neolithic Revolution: independent development of agriculture and animal domestication in several world regions beginning ~10,000 BCE / ~12,000 years ago
Consequences of farming: permanent settlements, food surplus, population growth, labor specialization, social hierarchy — setting the stage for the first cities
supporting: Earlier hominins (Homo erectus, Neanderthals) as context for Homo sapiens
Terms: Fertile Crescent, foraging, domestication, sedentism
Distinction between established fact (dates, sequence) and interpretation (why farming spread, its trade-offs)
outOfScope: The first cities and early river-valley civilizations in detail (owned by mesopotamia, ancient-egypt, ancient-china)
Modern agriculture and agronomy (owned by agriculture)

claims.claim: Anatomically modern Homo sapiens evolved in Africa. The Smithsonian dates this to about 300,000 years ago (reflecting fossils such as those from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco); some survey texts, including OpenStax, cite an earlier figure of roughly 200,000 years ago. The lesson gives the range ~300,000-200,000 years ago and attributes it.

Homo sapiens migrated out of Africa in a process spanning tens of thousands of years; OpenStax dates a major dispersal to approximately 100,000 years ago, reaching India and China by ~70,000 years ago, Australia/New Guinea by at least ~45,000 years ago, Europe by ~40,000 years ago, and the Americas by approximately 15,000 years ago. The Smithsonian gives a compatible sequence (Asia 80,000-60,000; Australia by 50,000; Europe by 40,000; Americas by 15,000 years ago).

During the Paleolithic (Old Stone) Age, humans lived in small nomadic bands (roughly 15-40 people) that survived by hunting and gathering, made and used stone tools, controlled fire (by at least ~125,000 years ago per OpenStax), and produced early art such as cave paintings.
The Paleolithic Age ended and the Neolithic Age began about 12,000 years ago (~10,000 BCE), coinciding with the end of the last ice age, when some populations adopted farming.

Agriculture and animal domestication developed INDEPENDENTLY in several regions at different times: the Near East/Fertile Crescent (wheat, barley, sheep, goats ~10,000-12,000 years ago), China (rice, millet, soybeans ~10,000 years ago), sub-Saharan Africa (sorghum, possibly ~6,000 years ago), Mesoamerica (maize/corn, squash), and South America (potatoes ~5,000 years ago). It was not a single event in one place.

Farming produced a reliable food surplus that supported larger, denser, permanent settlements (large settlements by ~9,000 years ago), population growth, and specialization of labor, and it restructured formerly egalitarian foraging societies into hierarchical ones with wealth differences.

These consequences of farming — surplus, sedentism, specialization, and hierarchy — set the stage for the first cities and civilizations, which are covered in later topics (Mesopotamia, Egypt, China).

conflictingEvidence.issue: The date at which anatomically modern Homo sapiens first appeared.
positions: Smithsonian Human Origins: ~300,000 years ago, reflecting fossils including Jebel Irhoud (Morocco).
OpenStax World History (2.1): 'modern humans emerged first in Africa approximately 200,000 years ago.'
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Present as a range (~300,000-200,000 years ago) and attribute; note that newer fossil finds pushed the estimate earlier. Do not state a single exact date.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Exact timing of the out-of-Africa migration.
positions: OpenStax: a major dispersal ~100,000 years ago.
Smithsonian: spread to Asia between 80,000 and 60,000 years ago.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Describe migration as a process over tens of thousands of years with approximate dates by region; the two sources give a compatible ordering of continents.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft contained only generic boilerplate ('Early Human Societies is a foundational concept in History...') with no factual content about prehistory, dates, migration, the Paleolithic, or the Neolithic Revolution. Nothing substantive to support or refute; discarded and rewritten.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced empty boilerplate with sourced content on human origins, out-of-Africa migration, the Paleolithic era, and the Neolithic Revolution.
Added explicit multi-region, independent-origins framing for agriculture (not a single Fertile Crescent event).
Gave dates as attributed ranges, not false precision, and flagged the 300,000 vs 200,000 year scholarly difference.
rightsIssues: OpenStax World History is CC BY 4.0 (attribution required); facts extracted and prose written originally. Smithsonian Human Origins used REFERENCE_ONLY for cross-checking dates; no Smithsonian wording reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: World History, Volume 1, to 1500 — 2.1 Early Human Evolution and Migration
sourceRecords.notes: Supports out-of-Africa migration dates (~100,000 years ago dispersal; India/China ~70,000; Australia ~45,000; Europe ~40,000; Siberia ~25,000; Americas ~15,000 years ago), the ~200,000-years-ago figure for modern human emergence, and context on Homo erectus and Neanderthals. Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19.

sourceRecords.title: World History, Volume 1, to 1500 — 2.2 People in the Paleolithic Age
sourceRecords.notes: Supports Paleolithic lifestyle: nomadic bands of ~15-40 people, subsistence hunting and gathering, stone tools, sewing needles by ~30,000 years ago, cave paintings/spirituality, control of fire by at least ~125,000 years ago, and the last ice age ending ~12,000 years ago. Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19.

sourceRecords.title: World History, Volume 1, to 1500 — 2.3 The Neolithic Revolution
sourceRecords.notes: Supports independent development of agriculture ~12,000 years ago across the Near East (wheat/barley), China (rice/millet/soybeans ~10,000 years ago), sub-Saharan Africa (sorghum ~6,000 years ago), Mesoamerica (maize), and South America (potatoes ~5,000 years ago); animal domestication (sheep/goats ~10,000, chickens ~8,000, horses ~6,000 years ago, llamas in Peru); and consequences: surplus, larger populations, permanent settlements by ~9,000 years ago, labor specialization, and social hierarchy. Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19.

sourceRecords.title: Homo sapiens — Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, Human Origins Program
sourceRecords.notes: Supports that Homo sapiens evolved in Africa about 300,000 years ago during dramatic climate change, and modern human anatomical features (large brain ~1300 cc, high-vaulted skull, reduced brow ridges). Used to cross-check and bracket the emergence date against OpenStax's ~200,000-year figure. No wording reproduced. Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19.

sourceRecords.title: Humans Change the World — Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, Human Origins Program
sourceRecords.notes: Supports the migration timeline (Asia 80,000-60,000; Australia by 50,000; Europe by 40,000; Americas by 15,000 years ago), symbolic behavior (recording information on objects by ~77,000 years ago; permanent drawings 60,000-40,000 years ago), and the transition from foraging to agriculture ~12,000 years ago. Used REFERENCE_ONLY to corroborate OpenStax. Read via WebFetch 2026-08-19.
